name: questing beast

attributes.attribute: hybrid body of serpent, deer, leopard
sound of thirty hooves when running
turned by the shock of his mother killed by wild dogs

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The questing beast, also called Beast Glatisant, is a monstrous creature in Arthurian legend. Its body blends one realm of a snake, a deer, and a leopard. It stands on only four legs. Each time it runs, the noise of thirty hooves rings out. A knight named as Pellinore or Palomides chases it without a fixed rest. Some stories say the beast was once a boy. He entered animal form after the shock, having seen his mother killed by wild dogs.

okr.objective: Describe the questing beast as a four-legged Arthurian hybrid and its tale of pursuit.
key_results: Record the beast as an Arthurian monster.
Detail its hybrid body of serpent, deer, and leopard with four legs and a thirty-hoof noise.
Give the chase by Pellinore or Palomides and the story of a boy turned to animal form.
